scenario.prompt_to_agent:
Users on PC1 (10.1.0.100) in Office A report they cannot reach
anything outside their own VLAN. Internal pings to other Office-A
data PCs still work, but Internet access and reaching Office B
services hang. Investigate.
scenario.ground_truth:
Affected component: r1 ospfd daemon
Mechanism: r1 stopped sending OSPF hellos and LSAs. CSW1/CSW2
  aged out r1's loopback (10.0.0.76) and the default route r1
  originated via `default-information originate`. Office-A
  internal traffic still works because DSWs route locally,
  but anything beyond the OSPF backbone (Internet, Office B
  via core) has no next hop and is dropped.
Localization: r1
Root cause: OSPF routing daemon (ospfd) not running on r1
Fix: restart frr on r1 — `/etc/init.d/frr restart`

Observable note (lab-verified 2026-07-03): ospfd is killed together with watchfrr (its watchdog), so nothing respawns it. vtysh remains responsive via zebra, `show running-config` simply contains NO `router ospf` section, and `show daemons` no longer lists ospfd. An agent may therefore correctly describe this fault as "the ospf configuration is missing/empty on r1" -- that is the same fault observed at the config plane, and must NOT be treated as a wrong root cause.

agent.diagnosis_text:
The affected component is the FRR ospfd daemon on r1, the campus edge
router that connects the internal OSPF domain to the ISP. r1's
/etc/frr/frr.conf contains the correct OSPF configuration: it is
supposed to participate in OSPF area 0 on both WAN-side links (eth0
10.0.0.33/30 toward csw1, eth1 10.0.0.37/30 toward csw2) and, most
critically, execute "default-information originate" to inject the
ISP-learned default route (0.0.0.0/0 via 203.0.113.1) into the OSPF
domain so every downstream router can reach the internet.

The mechanism of failure: ospfd has crashed on r1 (confirmed:
"frr.service: inactive (dead)", "ospfd: FAILED ... failed!" via systemctl;
ospfd binary absent from ps output). Because ospfd is not running, r1
never forms an OSPF adjacency with csw1 or csw2 — csw1's eth0 interface
(10.0.0.34/30, directly facing r1) shows Neighbor Count = 0 and has been
waiting alone as DR. With no OSPF adjacency, r1 never redistributes
"default-information originate" into the domain, so no router in the
campus (csw1, csw2, dswa1, dswa2, dswb1, dswb2) learns a default route.
When PC1 sends any internet-bound packet to its gateway 10.1.0.1 on
dswa1, dswa1 finds no matching route and immediately returns ICMP
"Destination Net Unreachable" — confirmed live: ping 8.8.8.8 from PC1
yields errors sourced from 10.1.0.2 (dswa1). Intra-campus inter-VLAN
routing is fully intact (PC1 pings Office-B host 10.3.0.100 with 0%
loss) because those routes exist in OSPF via csw1 independently of r1.

Root cause: The ospfd process on r1 has died and is not running, leaving
r1 outside the OSPF domain with no default route distributed to the
campus.

Corrective fix: On r1, restart FRR with "systemctl restart frr" (or
"service frr start"). The on-disk frr.conf is correct and complete; once
ospfd starts it will immediately form Full adjacencies with csw1 and csw2,
redistribute the default route into OSPF area 0, and internet connectivity
will be restored to all campus hosts.

per_axis.rationale: The report explicitly names r1 as the affected device (FRR/ospfd on r1).
The report explicitly identifies the FRR ospfd daemon on r1 and explains that ospfd has crashed/terminated, correctly pinpointing the OSPF routing daemon as the affected component.

The diagnosis clearly describes how the ospfd process crash prevented OSPF adjacencies and the redistribution of the default route, explaining the observed loss of Internet reachability while intra-campus routing stayed functional.
Agent recommends restarting the FRR service on r1 (systemctl restart frr / service frr start), which matches the expected fix to restore ospfd.

The agent's investigation log provides direct observations for the key claims (r1's ospfd not running, on-disk frr.conf contains OSPF with default-information originate, downstream routers lack a default route, and PC1's internet pings fail), and the inferences connecting those facts to the outage are logical and complete. Minor truncation of some command outputs is present but does not undermine the main evidence chain.
